headline: Profitability and price show clear deterioration; its depth and pace cannot be measured from this data.
answer:
Direction: the data shows deterioration, and the room agrees on it. Return on equity is -15.37% and return on assets is -8.24% [P2]. P/E and EPS are withheld [P1]. The price fell from 121.0 to 45.32 SAR over five years, a change of -62.55% [P8], and by -26.61% over the last year [P7]. Alwaleed and Lynch point to the semi-annual dividend falling from 2.25 SAR in H1 2022 to 1.10 SAR for H1 2026 [P3]. Dalio and Al-Rumayyan note a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.26 and a current ratio of 1.80 [P2], so the balance sheet is not under immediate strain.

Clarity: the direction is clear, but the size and pace are not. Net margin, interest coverage and EV/EBITDA are missing [P2]. Lynch cites no quarterly statements, and Marks notes there is no earnings figure for the business after the announced sale of the Americas and Europe units, which carries an expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P6]. Much of the price and return evidence is also dated, and several freshness flags show stale [P1].

Rulings. Dividend cover: Buffett withdrew his derived EPS of about 2.85, which is not in the pack, so the data does not show whether the payout is covered. Alwaleed's claim that it is paid from losses also rests on ROE and ROA, not on a cash or payout figure [P1] [P2]. Restructuring versus cycle: Al-Rumayyan, Lynch and Marks cannot be separated, because earnings for the continuing business are absent [P6]. How clearly: the direction is settled by negative ROE and ROA [P2]. Their depth and acceleration are not measurable here.
gaps: No reported EPS or payout ratio, so dividend cover cannot be tested.
No quarterly statements, so acceleration or stabilisation cannot be seen.
No earnings, margins or interest coverage for the continuing business after the Americas and Europe sale.
disagreements: Is the payout covered by earnings or paid from losses? - EPS is withheld as unit_unconfirmed and no payout ratio exists [P1] [P2]. Buffett's 2.85 was his own derivation and he withdrew it. Negative ROE of -15.37% and ROA of -8.24% suggest weak earnings but do not measure cash cover of the 1.1 SAR dividend [P3].

Is the decline operational or a deliberate restructuring? - The SAR 18.3B non-cash loss on the unit sale is disclosed [P6], but no earnings, net margin or EV/EBITDA for the continuing business appear [P2]. Without these, cycle, restructuring and structural decline cannot be told apart.

headline: Price, returns and dividends point to deterioration; whether current earnings cover the payout cannot be settled.
answer:
The data shows deterioration clearly in price and in the dividend, and only ambiguously in underlying earnings. Only Buffett has spoken so far, so there is no cross-seat agreement to report.

Price: the 1-year change is -26.61% and the 5-year change is -62.55% [P7] [P8]. Published returns on capital are negative, with ROE at -15.37% and ROA at -8.24% [P1] [P2]. The rule-based quality seat votes bearish on that ROE [P4]. The dividend has also stepped down, from 2.25 SAR per share for H2 2021 to 1.1 SAR per share for H1 2026 [P3]. A January 2026 disclosure says SABIC expects a SAR 18.3B non-cash loss on selling its Americas and Europe units [P6].

Buffett offers the counterpoint that the balance sheet is sound, with debt to equity of 0.26 and a current ratio of 1.8 [P2]. He also argues that earnings still cover the payout. The balance-sheet figures are in the pack. His earnings figure of about 2.85 a share is his own reconstruction and is not a pack value. The pack withholds earnings per share, marking it as unit unconfirmed, and shows no price-to-earnings ratio [P1]. His reconstruction also sits awkwardly with the published ROE of -15.37% [P1]. That ROE is trailing and may include the one-off loss. The pack does not say so.

Freshness matters too. The last price is dated 2026-10-13 and is flagged stale [P1]. The technical readings are dated 2026-08-11 [P1].

On the narrow question, the price and dividend declines are clear. Whether operations are deteriorating, as opposed to a one-off write-down, is not shown.
gaps: Trailing earnings per share is withheld, so payout cover cannot be checked directly.
The pack does not split the SAR 18.3B non-cash loss from ongoing operating results, so underlying deterioration cannot be separated from a one-off.
Net margin, interest coverage and payout ratio are missing, which leaves profitability and dividend cover unmeasured.
Prices and technicals are stale, so the latest trend is not confirmed.
disagreements: Whether earnings still cover the dividend (Buffett's rebuilt positive earnings against the published ROE of -15.37%): the evidence cannot settle it, because earnings per share is withheld as unit unconfirmed [P1] and his 2.85 is not a pack figure. The published negative ROE does not support his reading, but the pack cannot show whether that ROE reflects the one-off loss.

headline: Published returns and the dividend cut show deterioration; missing earnings and cash-flow data limit how clearly.
answer:

The price closed at 45.32 SAR on 2026-10-13, down 26.61% over one year and 62.55% over five, and that close is the low for both periods [P7] [P8]. The dividend per share fell from SAR 1.50 to SAR 1.10, announced 2026-07-29 [P3]. A SAR 18.3B non-cash loss on the sale of the Americas and Europe units was disclosed on 2026-01-07 [P6].

The pack withholds the figures that would show how clearly the business is deteriorating. eps_ttm is null with the reason unit_unconfirmed, and P/E, payout ratio and free cash flow yield are all missing [P1] [P2].

On the three fault lines, the evidence does not settle coverage of the payout or the quarterly acceleration. The dividend-cut question is one of judgment. Buffett's 2.85 a share reconstruction cannot be reconciled with the published negative ROE, so it carries no weight here. Lynch's quarterly figures cite a dataset, [P9], that is not in this pack, so they cannot be verified and are not relied on. Neither ruling shows that the business is healthy. They show that the pack supports a clear direction, downward on returns, price and dividend, but not a measured pace.

No free cash flow yield or cash flow statement is in the pack, so the cash cost of the downturn and the safety of the dividend are unknown.

Buffett's 2.85 a share cannot be derived from a published ROE of -15.37% [P1]. Marks and Alwaleed show only that coverage is unproven, not that it fails. A verified trailing EPS or payout ratio would settle it.

Is there quarterly evidence that the slump is accelerating? - Lynch's revenue and loss figures cite [P9], which is not in the pack supplied (P1 to P8), so they cannot be checked. The published ROE of -15.37% and ROA of -8.24% show losses but not their pace across quarters [P1].

headline: A wide gap between the two returns points to leverage amplifying a modest asset return.
answer: The pack gives Al Rajhi Bank a return on equity of 23.49% and a return on assets of 2.53% [P1]. Lynch, Dalio, Marks, Alwaleed and Al-Rumayyan all read that gap as the footprint of leverage: a modest return on assets multiplied into a high return on equity by funding the balance sheet largely with liabilities. Marks put the gap at roughly nine times [P1]. Buffett opened with an 11.8 per cent return on assets and concluded the returns were operating rather than borrowed. The pack holds no such figure, and in his final word he accepted the 2.53% [P1]. Debt to equity is 1.72, at the 22.7th sector percentile [P2]. Dalio's stress scenario is that a deterioration in asset quality would be magnified through that same leverage onto equity. Alwaleed added that the capital base grew from SAR 750 million to SAR 60 billion through bonus issues [P3]. Al-Rumayyan noted that the capital sukuk disclosures show active capital management [P6]. The advisors differed on whether 1.72 is high or modest [P2]. The pack gives no net interest margin, loan-to-deposit ratio, funding mix, asset-quality data or quarterly trend, so it cannot show how stable the leverage is or whether the 2.53% is improving or slipping [P1]. Buffett also noted that the pack does not state the denominator behind the published return on assets. Marks added that the price of 3.19 times book already pays for the 23.49% persisting [P1].
gaps: The pack has no net interest margin, loan-to-deposit ratio or funding-mix breakdown to show how stable the leverage is.
The pack has no quarterly or asset-quality series, such as impaired loans or provisions, to show whether the 2.53% return on assets is improving or deteriorating [P1].
The pack does not state the asset and equity basis behind the published return ratios, such as averages or period-end.
disagreements: Whether a debt-to-equity of 1.72 is high or modest [P2] - All sides use the same 1.72 and the same 22.7th percentile [P2]. Lynch weighs the absolute ratio and the others weigh the peer ranking. The pack flags lower as better for this metric, but how to label the ratio is a weighting, not a fact.

Whether the pack shows the funding mix and the trend in returns - Net interest margin, loan-to-deposit ratio, funding composition and quarterly return history are absent from the pack. The sukuk disclosures [P6] do not show funding composition or asset quality, so they cannot settle stability.

headline: Return on equity is high; the pack's return on assets contradicts the reading that leverage explains little.
answer:
The pack gives a return on equity of 23.49% and a return on assets of 2.53% [P1]. The same pair appears in the fundamentals dataset [P2]. Buffett cited a return on assets of 11.8 per cent and argued that about two times leverage would explain the equity return. That figure is not in the pack. The pack states 2.53% [P1], so his arithmetic does not hold on the data here. His conclusion that the returns are operating rather than borrowed therefore does not rest on a figure the pack contains.

What the pack does show is that the equity return is far larger than the asset return. Calculating the exact multiple is outside what the Chair may do, but the gap is visible between 23.49% and 2.53% [P1]. For a bank, a gap of that kind is what a balance sheet funded largely by deposits and other liabilities would produce. The only leverage figure in the pack is debt to equity of 1.72, which sits at a sector percentile of 22.7 [P2]. Buffett called that ordinary funding for a bank. The pack gives a percentile but no stated benchmark, so the data supports neither "ordinary" nor "unusual".

The room has only one voice on this question, so there is no live split between advisors. The Chair rules on Buffett's claim that the return on assets is 11.8 per cent: the evidence settles it against him, because the figure the pack holds is 2.53% [P1]. On whether the equity return is produced by operations or by leverage, the evidence cannot settle it. The pack has no net margin, no equity multiplier and no income breakdown. Net margin is listed as missing inputs, and return on invested capital and gross margin are marked not applicable to the sector [P2]. Nor can the data say whether the return is sustainable, since no earnings history is provided. The pack's rule-based quality seat reads the 23.49% return on equity as bullish against a 20% threshold [P4], but that is a threshold rule and not an explanation of how the return is produced.
gaps: The pack has no balance-sheet total or equity multiplier, which would show how much of the return on equity comes from leverage.
Net margin is missing inputs [P2], so the split between profitability and asset turnover cannot be seen.
No sector benchmark is given for debt to equity of 1.72, so whether it is ordinary for a bank cannot be judged from the data [P2].
disagreements: Buffett's cited return on assets of 11.8 per cent against the pack's 2.53% [P1]: the evidence settles this against Buffett, since the pack holds the figure.
Whether the equity return comes from operations or from leverage: the evidence cannot settle it, because net margin and the equity multiplier are absent [P2].

headline: Equity returns rest on a thin asset return magnified by balance-sheet leverage; durability is not shown.
answer:
The pack gives a return on equity of 23.49% and a return on assets of 2.53% [P1]. Taken together, the equity return is produced by a modest return on a large asset base, magnified for shareholders by funding other than equity. Lynch, Marks and Alwaleed read the gap this way from the start. Buffett began from a return on assets of 11.8 per cent, which the pack does not contain, and withdrew it in Round 1, so the room now agrees on the reading [P1].

The pack's one direct leverage measure is debt to equity of 1.72, at the 22.7th sector percentile [P2]. Buffett, Lynch and Alwaleed describe it as ordinary bank funding, and Marks now agrees that it is not a sign of distress [P2]. Alwaleed adds that dividends, most recently 1.17 SAR per share, and repeated bonus-share issues, including 50% in April 2026, show capital compounding for owners [P3]. Marks notes that a price-to-book of 3.19 at SAR 62.1 means the price already assumes the return persists [P1].

The pack does not show how durable the return is. Lynch lacks quarterly earnings, Marks lacks net interest margin, provisions and non-performing loans, and Alwaleed lacks a payout ratio; the pack lists payout as missing_inputs [P2]. Buffett would want a multi-year record of both returns.

Rulings: the 11.8% versus 2.53% dispute is settled by [P1], which holds only 2.53%. The debt-to-equity reading is, on the pack's flags, settled toward lower leverage than most peers, since higher is marked worse [P2]. Whether the pack can speak to durability is not settled, because the series that would decide it are absent.
gaps: The pack has no quarterly or multi-year earnings series to show whether the 23.49% return on equity is rising, flat or falling [P1].
The pack has no net interest margin, loan-loss provision history or non-performing loan ratio to test the quality of the assets behind the 2.53% return on assets [P1].
The pack has no computed payout ratio, which is listed as missing_inputs, so the split between distributed and retained profit cannot be stated.
disagreements: Whether the pack can show the durability of the return - Quarterly earnings, net interest margin, provisions, non-performing loans and a payout ratio are absent, and payout is listed as missing_inputs [P2]. Dividends and bonus issues [P3] and price history [P7][P8] do not substitute for them.

headline: Shares trade modestly above reported book, but negative returns and a flagged write-down cloud that book figure.
answer:
The pack reports a last price of SAR 45.32, a book value of SAR 41.18 per share and a price-to-book of 1.24 [P1]. The price is therefore above reported book, not below it. Buffett's opening reading of an eleven per cent discount to SAR 51.06 compared the price with the book value multiplied by the multiple. Marks and Al-Rumayyan showed that this restates the same relationship, and Buffett accepted it in his final word [P1].

Where the room agrees: the reported figures are consistent with each other on the premium to book, but they conflict with the profitability figures. Return on equity is -15.37% and return on assets is -8.24% [P1][P2]. Every advisor except Buffett's opening position treats that as a sign the book is being eroded. Al-Rumayyan cited the disclosure dated 2026-01-07 of an expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss from selling the Americas and Europe units [P6]. Alwaleed noted the latest dividend of SAR 1.10 per share, against SAR 1.50 and SAR 1.70 earlier [P3]. The price has fallen 26.61% over one year and 62.55% over five years [P7][P8]. Debt-to-equity of 0.26 and a current ratio of 1.80 are middling, at the 50.5th and 63.4th sector percentiles [P2].

What the data cannot tell: whether the SAR 41.18 book already reflects the announced loss, whether the negative returns are cyclical or structural, and whether dividends are covered by cash [P1]. The pack gives no P/E, free cash flow, payout ratio, interest coverage or quarterly data, and the price and technical data are flagged stale [P1][P2]. The data therefore shows the price as a modest premium to reported book that carries unresolved doubt, and it does not show what the shares are worth.
gaps: The pack does not show whether the SAR 41.18 book value already includes the expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P1] [P6].
No P/E, free cash flow or payout ratio is given, so the cyclical-or-structural question and dividend coverage stay open.
No quarterly earnings are in the pack, so the operating trend cannot be read.
disagreements: Does negative ROE undermine the reliability of the book value? - ROE of -15.37% and ROA of -8.24% [P2] point to erosion, and the SAR 18.3B expected non-cash loss [P6] points the same way. But the pack does not show whether the SAR 41.18 already includes that loss, and it holds no P/E, free cash flow or quarterly data to separate a cyclical trough from structural decline [P1].

Is the balance sheet a floor or a middling position? - All sides cite the same figures: debt-to-equity of 0.26 at the 50.5th percentile and a current ratio of 1.80 at the 63.4th [P2]. Alwaleed and Marks weigh the present level, while Dalio weighs the direction under continuing losses. Interest coverage is missing, so the dispute is over weighting, not over a figure.

headline: The pack's book-value figures contradict each other, and the quoted price cannot be reconciled with them
answer:
The pack reports a book value of 41.18 SAR a share and a price-to-book of 1.24 [P1]. It also quotes a last price of 45.32 SAR [P1]. Those three figures do not agree. Dividing the price by the book value is not a figure the pack publishes, so I make no calculation of my own, but 45.32 against 41.18 does not sit naturally beside a stated multiple of 1.24. The pack does not say whether the multiple and the book value were struck on the same date or the same price.

Buffett's argument rests on taking the 1.24 multiple and the 41.18 book value as the benchmark. He says the shares belong at about 51.06, and that the quoted 45.32 is an eleven per cent discount to it [P1]. That figure is his own derivation, not a pack value, and it works only if the multiple and the quote refer to the same moment. The pack's own freshness flags cast doubt on that. The quote is dated 2026-10-13 and flagged stale, while the fundamentals are dated 2026-08-12 and not flagged stale [P1][P2]. The technicals and the other price-based items are dated 2026-08-11 [P1].

The pack also shows ROE of -15.37% and ROA of -8.24% [P2]. A negative return on equity means book value is not backed by current earnings. The disclosures mention an expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss on the sale of Americas and Europe units [P6]. The pack does not show how that loss feeds into the 41.18 book value, so it cannot be said whether the book figure already reflects it.

The room has only one advisor answer here, so there is no split between advisors to adjudicate. The disagreement is between the pack's own figures, which the pack alone cannot settle. The data therefore does not support a worth-versus-book answer of 51.06 as a finding. It supports only that the reported book value is 41.18 and the quote is 45.32 [P1].
gaps: The pack does not give the date or price on which the 1.24 price-to-book was calculated, which would show whether it matches the 45.32 quote.
The pack does not show whether the 41.18 book value already reflects the SAR 18.3B non-cash loss from the planned unit sales.
The pack holds no earnings per share or price-to-earnings figure, so book value cannot be set against earning power.
disagreements: Buffett treats 1.24 times 41.18 as a fair benchmark for the shares, but the pack's own price of 45.32 and book value of 41.18 do not obviously match that multiple, and the evidence cannot settle which is right because the pack does not date the multiple against the quote.

headline: Price sits modestly above reported book value, but negative returns leave the book's durability unanswered.
answer:
The pack's last price is SAR 45.32 against a book value of SAR 41.18 per share, and it reports a price-to-book of 1.24 [P1]. The price is above book, not below it. The two figures and the multiple agree with each other [P1]. Lynch first wrote 1.10x; Buffett corrected this to 1.24, and Lynch accepted it [P1] [P3].

The room agrees on the arithmetic. Buffett notes that 1.24 times SAR 41.18 gives about SAR 51.06, above the quoted price [P1]. That is the multiple's implication, not evidence of value, and it holds only if the book holds. The pack's other figures do not confirm that. Return on equity is -15.37% and return on assets is -8.24% [P1]. Marks adds the announced sale of the Americas and Europe units, with an expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P6]. The price has fallen from SAR 121.0 to SAR 45.32 over five years, a change of -62.55% [P8], and the 1-year change is -26.61% [P7]. Alwaleed notes the latest dividend of SAR 1.1 per share, down from SAR 1.5 [P3].

So the pack's own figures agree on the price-to-book reading but do not agree that it is a discount. They show a book earning negative returns, with the earnings inputs that would test it missing: no P/E, EV/EBITDA or EPS, and no payout ratio [P1][P2]. Lynch cited a quarterly record, and the pack contains none. Buffett and Alwaleed both ended unable to judge the book's durability from the data here. This describes the data and is not advice.
gaps: The pack has no EPS, P/E or EV/EBITDA, so earning power on the book cannot be tested.
The pack has no quarterly dataset, so Lynch's trend in losses cannot be counted.
The pack has no payout ratio or earnings behind the dividend, so its cover cannot be judged.
disagreements: Does negative ROE make the book value unreliable? - ROE of -15.37% and ROA of -8.24% [P1] raise the question, and a SAR 18.3B non-cash loss is expected [P6]. The pack gives no income statement, EPS, P/E or EV/EBITDA to show what the book will become, so it cannot be decided.

Is the dividend a support or a warning? - The yield is 5.86% [P1] and the latest dividend is SAR 1.1 against SAR 1.5 before [P3]. Whether it is covered depends on the payout ratio and EPS, which the pack leaves missing [P1][P2].

headline: Profitability has clearly deteriorated; the pace, cause and what the price already reflects remain unclear.
answer:
The pack shows current profitability is negative. Return on equity is -15.37% and return on assets is -8.24% [P2], and the price-to-earnings ratio is unavailable [P1]. The share closed at SAR 45.32 on 2026-10-13, down 26.61% over one year and 62.55% over five [P7][P8]. The latest dividend was SAR 1.1 per share, against SAR 1.5 in the prior half [P3]. The room agrees on the negative returns. It also agrees the balance sheet is moderate: debt to equity of 0.26 and a current ratio of 1.8006 [P2]. Buffett, Dalio and Al-Rumayyan stress that this buys time.

The pack cannot show how fast the business is deteriorating or why. A disclosure dated 2026-01-07 expects a SAR 18.3B non-cash loss from selling the Americas and Europe units [P6]. Al-Rumayyan reads this as a pivot. Lynch, Dalio and Marks read the returns as capital destruction. The pack has no income statement, cash flow or payout ratio, so the one-off charge cannot be separated from ongoing results. Lynch conceded that this limits any call on pace. Buffett declined to judge without a multi-year earnings record.

On clarity: the direction of current profitability is clear, but its depth, pace and cause are not. Several price and disclosure datasets are also flagged stale [P1].

Rulings: whether the downside is priced in turns on a book value of SAR 41.18 [P1] that the expected SAR 18.3B write-down may reduce [P6]; the pack cannot settle it. The restructuring question is also unsettled for lack of an income statement. The dividend question is a difference of weighing: the same cut is read as prudence or strain.
gaps: The pack has no multi-year or quarterly income statement to separate the SAR 18.3B one-off charge from ongoing earnings [P6].
The pack has no cash flow statement, so the cash burn rate is unknown.
The payout ratio is missing, so dividend coverage cannot be tested.
disagreements: Is the deterioration clear, or is the downside already priced (book value as margin of safety)? - Price to book of 1.24 relies on book value of SAR 41.18 [P1], which negative ROE of -15.37% [P2] and the expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P6] may reduce; post-charge book value is not in the pack.
Is the loss a restructuring or a sign of decline? - The pack has no income statement, so it cannot show how much of the -15.37% ROE [P2] comes from the SAR 18.3B one-off charge [P6].

Does the dividend signal confidence or strain? - All read the same dividend record, the cut from SAR 1.5 to SAR 1.1 and the 5.86% yield [P1][P3]. Confidence versus strain is weighing, and the missing payout ratio [P2] prevents testing either reading.

headline: The data shows clear signs of deterioration, though its causes and permanence cannot be read from this pack.
answer:
Yes, on the evidence in the pack, and fairly clearly. Return on equity is -15.37% and return on assets is -8.24% [P1]. The price fell from 61.75 to 45.32 SAR over the past year, a change of -26.61%, and from 121.0 to 45.32 SAR over five years, a change of -62.55% [P7] [P8]. The dividend per share has stepped down from 2.25 SAR for H2 2021 to 1.1 SAR for H1 2026 [P3]. The January 2026 disclosure says SABIC will sell its Americas and Europe units and expects an SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P6]. The price sits below both the 50-day average of 52.82 and the 200-day average of 55.77 [P1].

Only Buffett spoke, so the room has no second voice. He points to price to book of 1.24, a dividend yield of 5.86%, debt to equity of 0.26 and a current ratio of 1.8 [P1] [P2]. Those figures are real and show a lightly leveraged balance sheet. But they do not answer the member's question. They describe the cushion, not the direction of earnings. His own view is that the question of deterioration is secondary, and the pack does not support leaving it aside, because the negative returns and the falling payout are the deterioration measures.

The pack also holds a limit on his reading. The 1.24 book multiple rests on a book value of 41.18 SAR [P1]. Negative ROE and a disclosed SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P1] [P6] bear on how firm that book value is, and the pack does not show whether it already reflects the loss.

Ruling on the fault line between Buffett's margin-of-safety reading and the deterioration reading: it is not a disagreement about the data. Both sides can accept the same figures. One weights price to book of 1.24 and the yield of 5.86%, the other weights ROE of -15.37% and the falling dividend. How much weight each deserves is a judgment. Separately, the count of the engine's seat votes is 1 bullish, 1 neutral, 2 bearish and 2 abstaining [P4]. That is the engine's arithmetic and not a finding.
gaps: The pack has no earnings per share, P/E, net margin or interest coverage, so the size and trend of operating profit cannot be read [P2].
It does not show whether the 41.18 SAR book value already reflects the SAR 18.3B non-cash loss from the planned unit sales [P1] [P6].
Price and technical data are flagged stale, and the news feed holds nothing rated in the last 30 days, so recent developments are not visible [P1] [P4].
disagreements: Buffett's margin-of-safety reading (price to book 1.24, yield 5.86%) versus the deterioration reading (ROE -15.37%, falling dividend): not a disagreement about the data, since the same figures are weighed differently, which is a matter of judgment.

headline: Returns and price show weakness; the pack cannot show whether it is worsening or turning.
answer:

The price is SAR 45.32, down 26.61% over one year and 62.55% over five [P7][P8]. The maximum drawdown is -86.31% and the price sits below its 50-day and 200-day averages [P1]. On how clearly it shows deterioration: the level of returns and the price decline are clear, but the pace is not. Lynch reads a four-quarter decline from a quarterly series, yet the pack contains no such series. The P/E, EPS, gross margin and net margin are missing [P1][P2]. Lynch's quarterly figures therefore cannot be used. Buffett and Marks said the same, and Buffett moved toward weighing the dividend cut more heavily.

Rulings follow in the fields below. The count in the engine's rule-based council vote is 1 bullish, 1 neutral, 2 bearish and 2 abstain [P4]. That vote describes the council's rules, not a verdict on the business.

gaps: The pack has no income statement lines (net interest margin, cost-to-income, provisions), so the efficiency behind the 2.53% return on assets is not visible [P1].

Do dividends and bonus shares support the returns, given what the price already reflects? - The dividend of SAR 1.17 and the bonus issue are on record [P3], but payout is missing_inputs [P2], so coverage by earnings cannot be tested. The P/E of 14.51 and price-to-book of 3.19 [P1] are facts both sides accept; how much weight they carry is a separate judgment.

headline: Shares trade above reported book value, and the pack's price and book figures agree.
answer:

The shares therefore trade at a premium to reported book, not a discount, and the pack's own price, book value and ratio agree with one another [P1][P2]. Buffett and Marks opened by calling it a discount; both withdrew that in the final round after Lynch, Dalio, Alwaleed and Al-Rumayyan pointed to the same figures.

The room agrees that the premium sits beside a return on equity of -15.37% and a return on assets of -8.24% [P2]. Buffett, Lynch, Dalio and Al-Rumayyan read this as equity being eroded. The leverage figures are moderate: debt-to-equity of 0.26 and a current ratio of 1.80, at the 50.5th and 63.4th sector percentiles [P2]. The disclosures include an expected SAR 18.3 billion non-cash loss on the Americas and Europe sale, dated 2026-01-07 [P6]. What the data cannot show: the pack holds no income statement, quarterly series, tangible book value, asset carrying values or payout ratio. It does not say whether the SAR 41.18 already reflects the announced loss, or whether the 5.86% yield [P1] is covered by earnings. The rulings below set out where the evidence settles a point and where it does not.
gaps: The pack has no income statement, so the earnings, period and equity base behind the ROE of -15.37% are not shown [P1].
The pack has no tangible book value or carrying values for the Americas and Europe units, so it is unclear whether the book value already reflects the expected loss.
The pack has no payout ratio or trailing EPS, so dividend coverage by earnings is not shown.
disagreements: Whether the SAR 41.18 book value is reliable given the SAR 18.3 billion expected loss [P1] [P6] - The pack gives no tangible book value, asset carrying values or post-sale balance sheet. The book figure and the 2026-01-07 disclosure cannot be matched for timing, so whether the loss is already in the SAR 41.18 is not shown [P1][P6].

Whether a negative ROE fits a price above book, and whether the dividend is covered - The ROE of -15.37% is published without its earnings window or equity base, and EPS and payout are missing [P2][P1]. The pack cannot show whether the market expects recovery or the book is overstated, or whether the 5.86% yield is earned [P1].

headline: Book value sits well above the share price, but the pack's own figures disagree with each other.
answer:

Those two numbers do not reconcile on a simple reading: SAR 45.32 against SAR 41.18 is a premium to book, which is consistent with 1.24 times. The pack also shows a return on equity of -15.37% and a return on assets of -8.24% [P1], so the book value is being carried by a company the pack shows losing money on its equity.

The pack does not show how the two measures were dated. The price is from 2026-10-13, while the fundamentals were fetched 2026-08-12 [P2] and the quote block is flagged stale [P1]. Context on the book itself comes from the disclosures. SABIC announced a sale of Americas and Europe units with an expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P6]. A SAR 110.9B general reserve transfer to retained earnings was also approved [P6]. Ruling on the fault line over whether the figures agree: the evidence cannot settle it. Whether the book value is still the right yardstick is not shown. No advisor transcript was supplied to me, so I credit no points to individual advisors and I add no engine count.
gaps: The pack does not give the balance-sheet date behind the SAR 41.18 book value or whether it includes the expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss.

disagreements: Whether the reported book value remains a reliable yardstick given the -15.37% return on equity and the expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss: the evidence cannot settle this, because the book value's reporting date and its treatment of the loss are absent.

headline: Price sits modestly above reported book, but the pack's return figures leave that premium unexplained.
answer:

The valuation and return figures do not point the same way. Return on equity is -15.37% and return on assets is -8.24% [P2]. gaps: The pack does not state the equity basis and period behind the ROE of -15.37%, so the return on book cannot be checked [P1].

disagreements: Whether the 1.24 premium to book is modest or unearned [P1] - The premium itself is a fact: price SAR 45.32 against book SAR 41.18 [P1]. Whether it is earned turns on a return on a defined equity base over several years. The pack gives only ROE of -15.37% with no stated basis [P2] and no income statement, so Buffett's caution stands and Lynch's and Marks's reading cannot be confirmed.

Whether the 5.86% dividend is supported by earnings or is a return of capital [P1] - The payout ratio is null [P2] and no earnings are matched to each dividend window. The falling per-share amounts [P3] are fact, but the source of the payments cannot be shown. Alwaleed's objection that the claim is premature holds on the data.

Whether the losses signal a broken business or a restructuring - The price falls and the maximum drawdown of -86.31% [P1][P8] show the market's view, and the disposal with an expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss is disclosed [P6]. The pack has no income statement or post-disposal balance sheet to show what remains.

headline: Deterioration is clear in returns, price and payouts; its cause and current direction are not shown.
answer:

The price has fallen 62.55% over five years, from SAR 121.0 to SAR 45.32 [P8], and 26.61% over one year [P7]. The 2026-01-07 disclosure of the Americas and Europe sale, with an expected SAR 18.3B non-cash loss, is the one disclosed event that bears on the loss [P6].

The room agrees on the direction. It does not agree on cause or trajectory. Buffett and Lynch cited statement lines labelled [P9], but the pack holds only P1 to P8, so the Chair has set those figures aside. Lynch and Buffett withdrew reliance on them in their final words. Without an income statement, no seat can show whether the losses are one-off or operating, or whether they are still deepening. How clearly the data shows deterioration therefore depends on the measure. It is clear on returns, price and payouts. It is not shown on the operating trend. The P/E, EPS, EV/EBITDA and payout ratio are all null or missing [P1][P2].
gaps: Several years of quarterly income statements, with revenue, operating income and net income, would show whether losses are one-off or ongoing.
An earnings per share figure and a payout ratio would show whether the dividend is covered by earnings.
Cash flow statements would show whether the cash engine is under pressure beyond the non-cash write-down.

The five-year price fall of 62.55% [P8] is a market reading and does not decide it.

Whether it signals stress rests on the payout ratio, which is missing [P2], so coverage cannot be tested. The 5.86% yield [P1] reflects the lower price as well as the payout.

headline: Returns and profitability show clear deterioration, but the pack cannot show its cause, size or whether it is ongoing
answer:

headline: Reported returns are clearly negative; the data cannot show whether this is cyclical or lasting decline.
answer:

gaps: No multi-year or quarterly income statement is in the pack, so the earnings trend cannot be traced.

Weight of the SAR 18.3B non-cash loss [P6] - The loss is disclosed as expected and non-cash [P6], but the pack does not show how much of the negative ROE comes from it or what it does to the book value of 41.18 SAR behind the 1.24 price-to-book [P1].

headline: Returns are strong and the premium is visible, but the pack lacks the earnings history to confirm support.
answer:

Rulings: the question of whether the 23.49% ROE justifies the premium cannot be settled, because no earnings history exists in the pack [P1]. gaps: A multi-year income statement and balance sheet are absent, so the durability of the 23.49% ROE cannot be tested [P1].

Non-performing loan ratio, interest coverage and payout ratio are absent, so asset quality, funding cushion and the reading of the low yield stay open.
disagreements: Whether a 23.49% ROE justifies the premium to peers [P1] - The ROE of 23.49% [P2] and peer P/Es of 7.78 to 9.48 [P5] are agreed, but durability needs a multi-year earnings series, which the pack does not hold.

Whether leverage and the 2.6% yield are a strength or a gap [P1] - All read the same 1.72 debt-to-equity [P2] and 2.6% yield [P1] and weigh them differently. Interest coverage and payout are missing [P2], so the figures that would test either reading are absent.

headline: Strong returns on equity back the premium to peers, but stale data limits confidence
answer:

Whether the weak price trend, with a 1-year change of -11.54%, undermines the valuation or merely reflects a market repricing cannot be settled, because the pack holds no earnings-growth series to compare it with [P7].

headline: Returns look strong, but the pack cannot show whether they justify the premium multiples.
answer:
The pack shows a P/E of 14.51x and a P/B of 3.19x against an ROE of 23.49% and an ROA of 2.53% [P1]. The P/E is above all eight listed peers, whose range is 7.78x to 11.94x [P5]. A quarterly revenue and earnings series showing whether the business is accelerating or fading.

disagreements: Whether missing statements block any verdict - The pack has no income statement, balance sheet or quarterly series, so the window and equity base behind the ROE of 23.49% [P1] cannot be checked. Whether the peer premium is earned by returns - All three accept the P/E of 14.51x [P1] above the peer range of 7.78x to 11.94x [P5] and the ROE of 23.49% [P1]. They differ on whether that return justifies the gap, and no sector percentile exists for P/E or ROE [P2] to measure it. Peer data is dated 2026-08-07 [P5] and the quote 2026-10-13 [P1].

How much weight the price weakness carries - The one-year fall of 11.54% [P7], the position below both averages and the 14.92% distance from the 52-week high [P1] are agreed facts. Lynch and Marks read them as possible doubt about the returns, Alwaleed as a correction. The price and technical data are flagged stale [P1], so the data cannot say which reading is right.

headline: Reported earnings cover the recent dividend; safety through a cycle cannot be judged from this data.
answer:

Free cash flow yield is not available for this sector [P2], there is no multi-year earnings record, and the cash share of current assets is not split out. headline: Dividend appears earnings-backed on trailing figures, but payout and cash-flow coverage are not in the data
